messages:
Ava: Heads-up: saw a customer report of transient double confirmed lines after a resume+toolcall sequence. Trace trc_z12.

Ravi: timeline?

Ava: client streamed prefix ~110 tokens, network hiccup, client resumed, router handed to a different backend, toolcall fired during resume, stream ended early. Ledger shows two provisional claims with identical prefix hash then two confirms, later reconciled into one usage (refund). Customer saw quota alert in the meantime.

Morgan: likely cause: provisional claims keyed to connection instance instead of resume_id. Router handoff lost parent_provisional context.

Ava: ledger snippet: [sanitized]
[2026-03-20T12:01:10Z] provisional p10 trace=trc_z12 tokens=55 hash=0x1a2b
[2026-03-20T12:01:13Z] handoff i-11 -> i-22
[2026-03-20T12:01:13Z] provisional p11 trace=trc_z12 tokens=55 hash=0x1a2b
[2026-03-20T12:01:15Z] confirm p10 -> cA tokens=55
[2026-03-20T12:01:16Z] confirm p11 -> cB tokens=55
[2026-03-20T12:01:20Z] reconcile merge cA,cB -> cA tokens=55 (refund issued)

Ravi: mitigation proposals: (1) router: forward resume_key/parent_provisional headers on handoff, (2) ledger: coalesce confirms by provisional-hash in a short grace window and atomically tombstone duplicates, (3) console: collapse provisional rows and mark as "may merge".

Morgan: prefer ledger coalesce + console collapse as quick wins, router header pass-through as longterm fix. Coalesce must set suppress_refund when tombstoning and attach merged_ids metadata. Use CAS on provisional-hash key to avoid concurrent confirm races.

Ava: agree. UX: show single provisional row with badge "merged provisional events" linking to trace. Add console filter to view only confirmed charges.

UIBot: Canary scheduled: ledger/coalesce -> 2026-03-21T02:30Z (canary: us-east-2 low traffic).

Ravi: action items: Ravi: ledger PR for confirm-coalesce + tests. Morgan: console collapse flag + small UX copy. Ava: coordinate canary and monitor provisional_merge_rate and transient_confirm_rows.

Ava: opening PRs and will paste links here. Thanks.
